subject: PO vs Card for Redwood - procurement readiness and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa@finopsco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood follow-up: procurement path (PO vs card) + next steps

Hi Lisa,

Thanks again for taking time today - great to learn more about FinOpsCo's rollout plans. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Procurement posture: you mentioned AP prefers POs for vendors and that new vendors need vendor onboarding + W-9 before PO issuance.
- Commercial path options:
  - Self-serve/credit card: fastest if you want to start immediately, but you noted card spend caps for new projects.
  - PO/net terms: requires vendor onboarding and internal approvals (2-3 week typical SLA per your note).
- Technical: we confirmed no IP transfer required and standard data residency is fine for this project.

Next steps I propose:
1) I can send our vendor onboarding packet and a PO template for your AP team to review (attached).
2) If you want to start sooner, we can temporarily provision a short-term card purchase for an initial pilot while onboarding completes - small pilot package (up to $5k).
3) Lauren (cc'd) can join the procurement thread if you want to coordinate the vendor forms.

Please confirm which path you prefer (card pilot vs wait for PO) and whether procurement wants the questionnaire + PO template.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: vendor_onboarding_questionnaire.pdf, PO-template.xlsx

From: Lisa Park <lisa@finopsco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finopsco.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:37:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood follow-up: procurement path (PO vs card) + next steps

Hi Marissa - thanks for the clear recap.

Short answers:
- AP policy: we generally require vendor onboarding + W-9 before issuing a PO. Exceptions for card spend need finance approval and are limited to <$2k per vendor for pilots.
- Timeline: vendor onboarding + approvals usually take 7-14 business days once forms are submitted.

Can you send over the onboarding packet and the PO template (I see you attached them - we'll pull into our system). Procurement is looped (procurement@finopsco.com) for intake.

Given the finance cap, the $5k card pilot would need additional sign-off. For speed, we can:
1) Submit the vendor packet and try to expedite PO for an initial quarterly commit, or
2) Start with a smaller card purchase under $2k and expand after PO.

I'll review the questionnaire with procurement and get back with a preferred path by EOD Friday.

Regards,
Lisa
Director of Finance, FinOpsCo
lisa@finopsco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700

Thanks Lisa - that all makes sense. A couple quick clarifications so procurement has everything they need: 

- Vendor packet includes: W-9, standard MSA (redlines typically limited to scope/SOW and liability caps), security questionnaire stub, and PO billing terms.
- PO template: includes billing contact (accounts-payable@redwood.com), remit address, and our tax info.

If procurement wants to accelerate, we can:
- Provide a redline-ready MSA and a short SOW to limit legal review time, or
- Offer a 30-day pilot contract addendum to get you running while PO completes (this is common for early pilots).

I've attached the onboarding packet and PO template again. Lauren, would you be able to drop the MSA/short SOW into a Drive link and share with procurement if they request it?

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
